macro: Chicago-area manufacturing activity contracted sharply in August, with the Chicago Business Barometer collapsing to 47.1 from 57.6, a 10.5-point drop that missed the 57.8 consensus by the widest margin of the year. The move came alongside a softer Conference Board confidence reading and adds to a mixed data picture the Fed weighs into its September 15-16 meeting, where futures markets are pricing meaningful odds of a rate move. Core CPI held at 2.5% year-over-year in July, still above the Fed's 2% target, while headline inflation ran at 3.4%. The week's most important data point is Friday's August nonfarm payrolls report, with consensus at +73,000 jobs and unemployment expected to tick up to 4.3% from July's 4.1%.

energy: WTI crude rose 0.94% to $86.57 a barrel and Brent gained 0.87% to $91.28, both climbing after U.S. forces struck Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island and Iran retaliated against targets in the UAE and Jordan, with Washington extending threats to Kharg Island, Iran's main export terminal. EIA data for the week ended August 21 showed a modest 0.1-million-barrel inventory build, leaving stocks about 1% above their five-year average even as Gulf shipping remains severely disrupted.
vix_and_dollar: The VIX closed at 14.92 on August 31, still in calm territory (below 15) despite a 3.4% daily rise. The dollar index is falling, down to 99.56 and on pace for a second straight monthly loss even as rate-hike odds build — a combination that suggests risk appetite is holding up despite the volatility uptick.
mortgage_rate: The 30-year fixed mortgage averaged 6.66% in Freddie Mac's survey for the week of August 27, 2026, essentially flat versus the prior week's 6.65%. Rates near this level continue to weigh on affordability even as the national Housing Affordability Index improved to 103.3 in July from 98.3 a year earlier.
personal_finance_deep_dive: The Conference Board's Expectations Index — which measures households' six-month outlook on income, business conditions and the labor market — fell 5.8 points to 68.2 in August, well below the 80 threshold that has historically preceded a recession within a year. Respondents cited energy costs, geopolitical tensions and employment concerns more often than a month earlier. The headline confidence index also missed forecasts, falling to 89.4 versus 90.3 expected, even as the Present Situation Index actually improved 6.8 points — a split that suggests households are more worried about where things are headed than where they stand today.
wealth_building_deep_dive: Fidelity's Q1 2026 retirement analysis found 645,000 401(k) accounts have crossed the $1 million mark, up 26% from a year earlier even after a 3% quarterly dip. The combined employee-employer 401(k) savings rate also hit a record 14.4%, nearing Fidelity's recommended 15% target. The through-line is consistency: the millionaire accounts skew toward savers who kept contributing through multiple downturns rather than timing entries and exits. A saver earning $70,000 who raises their contribution rate by even 2 percentage points and leaves it alone captures the same compounding effect at a smaller scale.
